entries.name: orchestrator-agent

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 20 Mon — Orchestrator agent (multi-module project).

Top-level entry-point that takes a natural-language feature
spec + runs the full Architect → Coder → Code-reviewer chain
end-to-end.  This is the v0.3 headline demo: a single
`aislang chat full_design examples/agents/orchestrator/`
invocation drives a 3-agent pipeline against the user's
local Ollama (qwen3:8b + qwen2.5-coder:7b) + emits a
structured design + Rust patch + reviewer verdict.

## Direct chat

```
aislang chat full_design examples/agents/orchestrator/
> Design a `dataset` block for declaring training data
  (path + format fields, fits the existing v0.3 grammar).
```

The CLI's pipeline-label dispatch (Week 17 Thu) drives the
runtime patterns::orchestrator::run — each step's output
feeds the next step's input verbatim.

## Coder ↔ Reviewer reflector loop (grammar layer)

`loop.review_cycle` wraps `pipeline.coder_review_cycle` with a
`condition` that re-runs the pipeline while the reviewer's
verdict does NOT start with `ACCEPT`, hard-capped at 3 retries.
This is the FIRST .ais-grammar-layer expression of the
reflector pattern from Week 17 Fri — runtime dispatch via
`loop`-block label is a follow-up (today Mon ships the
grammar + a runtime integration test exercising the parsed
loop AST through `patterns::reflector::run` with mocked
sub-agent dispatch + the `max_iter` hard-cap honoured).

## Cross-module composition

Sibling modules under `../architect/`, `../coder/`,
`../code_reviewer/` are referenced via `use <module>.<label>`
(Decision 44.1).  Each sibling is a self-contained
`project { … }` block (the Week 19 single-file agents);
the multi-module resolver merges all four projects' resource
namespaces at validate time + this module's pipelines refer
to the merged labels with the `use` prefix.

entries.name: patterns-router-demo

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 17 Fri — worked router-pattern demo.

Three-way customer-support router: each user message goes through
a classifier agent that picks one of {billing, technical, general},
and the matched case's pipeline handles the actual reply.

  user → classifier → case key → matched pipeline → answer

## Why router (not orchestrator)?

Orchestrator chains agents UNCONDITIONALLY — every message visits
every step.  Router DISPATCHES: each message visits exactly ONE
case-pipeline (chosen by the classifier), keeping latency + cost
down when the case-pipelines are heavyweight.  Use the router
when handling distinct workloads under one chat surface (a
customer-support intake, a routing dispatcher, a question-typing
triage).

## v0.3 classifier-agent convention

v0.3 Fri's CLI uses the project's FIRST declared agent as the
router's classifier.  We declare `agent "classifier"` first
here for that reason; it's a toolless agent whose prompt is
tuned to emit the case key only.  (v0.5+ may add an explicit
`classifier = agent.<label>` field in the `branch { … }` block;
until then the source-order convention rules.)

## Run it

```
aislang apply examples/patterns/router-demo/router-demo.ais       # bring stack up
aislang chat triage examples/patterns/router-demo/router-demo.ais

> How do I reset my password?
 · router classifying via agent `classifier` against cases [billing, general, technical]
 · router → case `technical` (1 steps)
 · orchestrator step 1/1 → agent `technical`
You can reset your password from the login page → "Forgot password"
link.  We'll email you a reset link valid for 30 minutes.

> How do I update my payment method?
 · router → case `billing` (1 steps)
 · orchestrator step 1/1 → agent `billing`
You can update your payment method in your account settings under
Billing → Payment Methods.  Changes apply to your next invoice.

> Hi!
 · router → case `general` (1 steps)
 · orchestrator step 1/1 → agent `general`
Hello!  How can I help today?
```

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 17 Thu — worked orchestrator-pattern demo.

Two-agent pipeline that exercises the orchestrator composition
primitive end-to-end:

  1. `researcher` — reads /data/company-info.md (via mcp_server.docs
     bind-mounted from ./knowledge/) and returns the raw fact set.
  2. `summarizer` — takes the researcher's raw output and produces
     ONE concise sentence.

The pipeline `research_then_summarize` chains them sequentially:
each user message dispatches step 1 with the user's query → step 1's
reply becomes step 2's input → step 2 produces the final answer.

Run it:

```
aislang apply examples/patterns/orchestrator-demo/orchestrator-demo.ais   # bring stack up
aislang chat research_then_summarize examples/patterns/orchestrator-demo/orchestrator-demo.ais
> Where is Acme headquartered?
 · orchestrator step 1/2 → agent `researcher`
   [researcher reads company-info.md, returns relevant facts]
 · orchestrator step 2/2 → agent `summarizer`
   [summarizer condenses to one sentence]
Acme Demo Company is headquartered in Berlin, Germany.
```

You can also chat the individual agents directly:

```
aislang chat researcher  examples/patterns/orchestrator-demo/orchestrator-demo.ais
aislang chat summarizer  examples/patterns/orchestrator-demo/orchestrator-demo.ais
```

— useful for debugging which step's behaviour you want to tune.

entries.name: portfolio-pnl

docs.header:
portfolio-pnl — a local-first, multi-agent portfolio analysis app.

Topology (see DESIGN.md § "Skills vs. agents"): the deterministic
stages are aiSlang `skill` blocks — the language model never fetches
or does the math. The judgement stages are LLM agents that INTERPRET
the computed JSON, grounded by a RAG knowledge corpus (Taleb
anti-fragility + re-balancing heuristics under ./knowledge/):

  • Strategic    — reads the analyze JSON, assesses anti-fragility.
  • Orchestrator — turns that brief into a keep/rebalance call.

── Run it ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deterministic core (no LLM needed):
  aislang skill run fetch_prices examples/portfolio-pnl/portfolio.ais
  aislang skill run analyze      examples/portfolio-pnl/portfolio.ais
  # or fully offline:  python3 scripts/seed_demo.py && python3 scripts/analyze.py --persist

The agents (needs a chat model + Ollama bge-m3 for the RAG index):
  ./run.sh                       # fetch → analyze → pipe into `advise`
  # or by hand:
  aislang chat advise examples/portfolio-pnl/portfolio.ais
  # then paste the analyze JSON as the first turn.

entries.name: qwen-smoke

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 18 Fri — worked Qwen-on-Ollama smoke demo.

Pins the two new local-LLM catalog entries shipped Fri:

  - `ollama.qwen3_8b`           → litellm tag `ollama/qwen3:8b`
  - `ollama.qwen2_5_coder_7b`   → litellm tag `ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b`

Both are FREE (local) — no API key needed; the Compose stack only
needs `OLLAMA_API_BASE` pointing at an Ollama daemon that's
already pulled the matching tag.  On the development rig this
resolves to `http://server.local:11434` (see `.env`); on a
laptop with `ollama` running locally it's `http://host.docker.
internal:11434`.

## Why Qwen3 8B and not 7B (per the PLAN row)

Ollama publishes qwen3 in 0.6b / 1.7b / 4b / 8b / 14b / 32b
sizes — NO 7b tag.  The closest cousin still on a consumer-GPU
VRAM budget (q4_K_M ≈ 4.5 GB) is 8b.  Decision 44.8 notes
"Both fit on consumer GPUs (12-24 GB VRAM)"; 8b is well under
the lower end of that range so the spirit of the choice is
preserved.

## Two agents — same model class, different role

  - `agent.thinker` uses `model.qwen3` — general-purpose
    analytical chat (reasoning-capable per the catalog entry).
  - `agent.coder`   uses `model.qwen2_5_coder` — coding-focused
    fine-tune of Qwen2.5 (HumanEval leader at the 7B scale per
    Decision 44.8).

## Run it

```
aislang apply examples/qwen-smoke/qwen-smoke.ais

# Reasoning smoke against Qwen3:
aislang chat thinker examples/qwen-smoke/qwen-smoke.ais
> Say hello in 5 words.
> /exit

# Coding smoke against Qwen2.5-Coder:
aislang chat coder examples/qwen-smoke/qwen-smoke.ais
> Write a Rust fn that returns the sum of integers from 1 to n.
> /exit

aislang destroy examples/qwen-smoke/qwen-smoke.ais
```

entries.name: template-demo

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 18 Tue — worked dynamic-prompts demo.

Pins the `prompt "<l>" { template = true }` flag end-to-end:

  1. `agent.static_explainer`  uses `prompt.static_sys`  — plain
     text body; passed to the LLM verbatim (v0.2-equivalent path).
  2. `agent.dynamic_explainer` uses `prompt.dynamic_sys` — body
     contains `{{ agent }}`, `{{ model }}`, `{{ prompt }}`
     variables AND a `{% if model == "thinker" %}…{% endif %}`
     control-flow block.  The runtime renders the file as a
     MiniJinja template at chat-turn time, substituting the
     built-in context built from the (agent, prompt, model)
     triple.

## What this demo proves at runtime

  - `aislang chat dynamic_explainer …` → system prompt the LLM
    sees has `agent=dynamic_explainer`, `model=thinker`,
    `prompt=dynamic_sys` substituted into the body (verifiable
    via Jaeger: open the `aislang.turn` span, inspect the
    `aislang.system_prompt` attribute — substitutions visible).
  - `aislang chat static_explainer …` → byte-stable v0.2
    behaviour; the LLM sees `prompts/static_sys.md` verbatim.
  - The control-flow `{% if model == "thinker" %}` block emits
    a different paragraph depending on which model the agent
    resolves to — change the agent's `model = model.X` ref to
    try both arms without editing the prompt.

## Run it

```
aislang apply examples/template-demo/template-demo.ais

# Template-enabled agent — ask about its identity:
aislang chat dynamic_explainer examples/template-demo/template-demo.ais
> Which model are you running on?
I'm running on model `thinker`.
> Which agent are you?
I'm the `dynamic_explainer` agent.

# Static-prompt agent — same question, doesn't know:
aislang chat static_explainer examples/template-demo/template-demo.ais
> Which model are you running on?
I don't know — my system prompt is plain static text...
```

entries.name: comment-clamper-agent

docs.header:
v0.4 Week 26 Mon — comment-clamper dogfood agent.

Mission soft-pref "agents author v0.4 code": an aiSlang agent that
CLAMPS the codebase's verbose doc-comments (the long Decision-46.x
narrations + PLAN-style day-row notes that accreted across the build)
down to a budget, WITHOUT changing code or losing load-bearing
meaning (Decision refs, invariants, the "why" behind a non-obvious
choice).  Run over `crates/aislang-cloud/` as the W26 Mon refactor's
comment pass.

## Direct chat (one comment block at a time)

```
aislang chat comment_clamper \
  examples/agents/comment_clamper/comment_clamper.ais
> <paste a verbose /// doc-comment or //! module header>
```

The agent returns ONLY the clamped comment (same `///` / `//!` / `//`
prefix), ready to paste back over the original.  It never emits code,
never invents Decision numbers, and keeps every reference that was in
the input.

## Model choice

anthropic.claude_haiku_4_5 primary — clamping is a bounded
summarization task (fast tier is plenty); ollama qwen3:8b fallback
for the offline/CI case.

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 20 Wed — DB agent.

Frames the v0.3 dogfood target — SQLite-based unification of
the v0.2 plain-files store (`~/.aislang/spend.json` +
`<source_dir>/.aislang/state.json` + per-project
`aislang.lock` mirrors) into a single `~/.aislang/store.db`.
Originally tracked as v0.2 DoD #7 (Centralized
`~/.aislang/store.json`) + scope-revised at v0.2 close to
land via the DB-agent dogfood here.  See PLAN-v0_3.md
Week 20 Wed row + PLAN-90-days-v0_2.md DoD #7 note.

## Direct chat (refine the migration brief)

```
aislang chat db examples/agents/db/db.ais
> Outline the v0.3 SQLite store migration.  Cover the three
  current plain-file sources + the reversibility contract.
```

The DB agent emits a **Feature spec** in the same shape the
Architect expects as input — the standalone chat is for
iterating on the migration brief before handing it to the
orchestrator.

## Hand off to the orchestrator (Thu dogfood)

Once the Feature spec is shaped to your liking:

```
aislang chat full_design examples/agents/orchestrator/
> /paste
<paste the DB-agent's Feature spec output>
/end
```

…and the orchestrator chain runs Architect → Coder →
Code-reviewer → Tester end-to-end against the migration
spec.  Wed ships the DB agent + the migration brief
corpus; Thu's dogfood-validation row exercises the full
chain (see PLAN-v0_3.md Week 20 Thu).

## RAG context

`knowledge = [vector_store.db_kb]` — current spend.json /
state.json / aislang.lock schemas + the proposed SQLite
tables + the Decision-44.4 byte-stability + reversibility
contracts.  Grounds the agent so it doesn't invent a
schema that loses today's audit-trail fields.

## Model choice

Cloud-tier reasoning model (Haiku) primary, matching the
Architect / Reviewer / Tester choice from Mon-Tue.  Brief-
writing is judgement work (which fields are load-bearing
for v0.2 round-trip?  which v0.5+ extensions should we
leave hooks for?), not code emission.  qwen3:8b stays as
the local fallback for the GPU case.

entries.name: rag-demo

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 19 Wed — worked RAG demo end-to-end against bge-m3.

Pins the Mon→Tue→Wed Decision-44.6 chain via four pieces:

  1. `embedding "local_bge"` — declares Ollama's bge-m3
     embedding model (1024-dim dense output, 8k ctx).
  2. `vector_store "aislang_docs"` — bind-mounts `./knowledge/`,
     chunks at 512 chars with 64-char overlap, embeds via
     embedding.local_bge.
  3. `agent "doc_helper"` — declares
     `knowledge = [vector_store.aislang_docs]` so Phase 2's
     chat-time prepend hook will auto-include retrieved chunks
     in the system prompt.
  4. (Today) `aislang rag query aislang_docs <demo> "<question>"`
     drives the build_index + query round-trip directly + prints
     the top-K matching chunks.

## Run it

Prereqs: `ollama pull bge-m3:latest`; LiteLLM stack up
(`aislang apply examples/rag-demo/rag-demo.ais`).

```
# Build the index (chunks ./knowledge/, embeds each chunk via
# ollama/bge-m3 through LiteLLM, persists to .aislang/vector/
# aislang_docs.bin):
aislang rag build aislang_docs examples/rag-demo/rag-demo.ais

# Query — embeds the question + returns top-3 chunks by cosine
# similarity:
aislang rag query aislang_docs examples/rag-demo/rag-demo.ais \
    "How does aislang ship RAG?"
# → [0] score=0.78  | # RAG resources (v0.3 Week 19) ...
# → [1] score=0.42  | ...
# → [2] score=0.31  | ...

aislang rag query aislang_docs examples/rag-demo/rag-demo.ais \
    "What runs on Kubernetes?"
# → [0] score=0.71  | # Kubernetes deployment (v0.2 Phase 2) ...
```

## v0.3 limitations exercised by this demo

  - **chunk_size is CHARACTERS, not tokens** (v0.3
    simplification — see LANGUAGE-SPEC §4.15).  bge-m3's 8k
    context window is more than enough for our 512-char chunks.
  - **Brute-force cosine scan** instead of usearch (Decision
    44.4 deviation; documented in rag.rs module head).
    Performance is fine for this 4-doc corpus + would scale to
    thousands of chunks before the linear scan matters.
  - **No agent.knowledge wiring in chat path yet** — the
    `doc_helper` agent declares `knowledge = …` but the chat-
    time auto-prepend of retrieved chunks to the system prompt
    lands in Phase 2 alongside the dogfood agent inventory.
    For now, `aislang rag query` exposes the retrieval surface
    directly.

entries.name: skill-demo

docs.header:
v0.3 Week 18 Wed-Thu — worked `skill { … }` block demo.

Wed shipped the grammar (parser + checker + LANGUAGE-SPEC §4.12);
Thu shipped the runtime (`aislang-runtime::skills::{run_shell_skill,
run_mcp_skill}`).  This file exercises BOTH execution modes end-
to-end via the new `aislang skill run` CLI subcommand.

## Skill blocks declared here

  - **`echo_greeting`** — shell-exec; output_type = string.
    Trivial round-trip — prints a fixed greeting.  Useful as a
    smoke test that the per-skill sandbox is wired (cwd, scrubbed
    PATH).

  - **`describe_self`** — shell-exec; output_type = json.
    Emits a JSON object via stdout; runtime parses + surfaces
    as `SkillOutput::Json`.

  - **`list_cwd_files`** — shell-exec; output_type = list_string.
    Lists everything in the per-skill sandbox cwd (`<project>/
    .aislang/skills/list_cwd_files/`).  First run shows the dir
    empty; rerun-after-touching-a-file shows the new entries.
    Demonstrates that the sandbox dir is persistent across runs
    (useful for skills that want to cache state).

  - **`evil_sudo`** — shell-exec; output_type = string.
    Tries to run `sudo cat /etc/shadow`.  The runtime's pre-flight
    denylist (`SkillError::DeniedCommand`) blocks it BEFORE
    spawning — no process ever runs.  Demonstrates the v0.3 Thu
    sandbox's deny posture.  Expected to FAIL with exit 1.

  - **`read_notes`** — MCP delegate; output_type = string.
    Calls `read_text_file` on the bundled `mcp/filesystem` MCP
    server (same image agent.tools = [mcp_server.docs] would
    use).  Demonstrates that an `mcp_server` block can back BOTH
    an agent's tool fleet AND a skill — single container, no
    duplicate spawn.  Requires Docker.

## Run them

Build the binary first (release):

```
cargo build --release --bin aislang
```

### Shell-exec skills (no infra needed)

```
./target/release/aislang skill run echo_greeting    examples/skill-demo/skill-demo.ais
# → hello from the aislang skill runtime

./target/release/aislang skill run describe_self    examples/skill-demo/skill-demo.ais
# → {"runtime":"aislang","mode":"shell","sandbox":"per-skill"}

./target/release/aislang skill run list_cwd_files   examples/skill-demo/skill-demo.ais
# → (empty list on first run; populates after touching files
#    in `.aislang/skills/list_cwd_files/`)

./target/release/aislang skill run evil_sudo        examples/skill-demo/skill-demo.ais
# → ERROR (exit 1): skill `evil_sudo` shell command denied: matched
#   pattern `sudo ` (denylist policy — v0.3 Thu sandbox; ...)
```

### MCP-delegate skill (requires Docker)

The `mcp/filesystem:1.0.2` image bind-mounts `./knowledge/` from
the project into the container's `/projects/`; pass the path the
tool sees as JSON args:

```
./target/release/aislang skill run read_notes \
    examples/skill-demo/skill-demo.ais \
    --args '{"path":"/data/notes.md"}'
# → <the contents of examples/skill-demo/knowledge/notes.md>

(The aislang `mcp_server.mount` field bind-mounts `./knowledge/`
at `/data/` inside the container — see `aislang-runtime::mcp::
config` for the wire shape.)
```
